sources: Sources: official airport weather reports (9:00 AM) and airport forecasts (issued 7:00 AM) from aviationweather.gov for 10 airports. The other 26 airports have no official airport report, so they use the MET Norway location forecast (updated 9:16 AM) and are marked Estimate. Estimates show rain and wind only and cannot confirm thunderstorms, so an Estimate airport is never shown as Danger. For Estimates, bad weather means moderate or heavy rain (2.5 mm or more in an hour), or winds of 39 km/h or more. Tomorrow and days-ahead outlooks use the same airport forecasts and MET Norway estimates and are less certain than today's alerts. Typhoon watch compares three sources, checked 9:52 AM: aviation storm warnings (position, movement, warning areas), RSMC Tokyo of the Japan Meteorological Agency (strength, how far strong winds reach, 24-hour forecast) and GDACS (cross-check). Reached at this check: aviation storm warnings, RSMC Tokyo, GDACS. A cyclone is shown and alerted only when at least two of them report it. Earthquakes are from USGS (magnitude 4.5 and stronger), data as of Nov 17, 9:52 AM. Accuracy ranking, highest first: 1) official airport report, 2) official airport forecast, 3) official aviation area warning, 4) computer forecast estimate. The moving rain layer on the map is a MET Norway forecast, rebuilt every few hours; it is a picture of the forecast and plays no part in the alert levels. When sources differ the higher-ranked one is used, and each airport's details show its confidence. If a source cannot be reached, its backup is used automatically and the Data sources table shows which one supplied the data. Times are Philippine time. Volcanoes: ash clouds and eruptions are from official aviation ash warnings (SIGMET) on aviationweather.gov, checked 9:52 AM. Volcano alert levels are from PHIVOLCS volcano bulletins.
